children: The death toll from the September 30 fire at MRPLc’s (Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd) coker hydrotreater unit in phase III rose to two after another contract employee succumbed to injuries on October 17.

One person was killed and 12 injured in the incident on September 30. Of the 12 injured, Rajesh D’Silva, a contract employee, was admitted to hospital with 35 per cent burns on that day. Police said he succumbed to injuries on October 17.
Others with minor injuries had received outpatient treatment on September 30.

The company had earlier said that an incident involving the rupture of a cold separator operating at high pressure in the coker hydrotreater unit resulted in a fire on September 30. The battery limits of the affected unit were immediately isolated to control the situation.

In its notes to the standalone financial results for the second quarter of 2026-27, the company had informed stock exchanges that it has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the September 30 fire incident at ₹118.76 crore.

“Based on a preliminary assessment, the company has provisionally estimated the financial impact of the incident at ₹118.76 crore, comprising the estimated carrying value of the damaged Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), corresponding to an estimated replacement value of approximately ₹225 crore and losses relating to inventories and other incidental expenses,” it said.
The company said the affected assets are adequately insured by it.

title: Death toll in Sept 30 MRPL fire rises to 2
